Repair the observed visibility failures in the same independently authored autumn-fashion rooftop theatre moment. The closed retry context preserves seasonal theme, human subject, reference cues, action, material/appearance meaning, setting and the selected four-component garment-fold obligation. A slight upper-body and elbow rotation and a front three-quarter view expose the existing sleeve seam and the canvas path through the ring. The outfit and same practical purpose remain authorial retained choices, not new requester definitions. Open choices are restricted to the coordinator-approved working-arm pose, local hand contact, camera direction, contact/outfit framing and occlusion. At the unchanged sensual 1, retain quiet everyday attraction through attentive presence; fetish and surreal remain 0 and creativity remains 1. Compare a side-led attachment view with a slightly more frontal working view: the latter keeps the same task while exposing the ring opening, elbow seam and waist landmark, so it is chosen.

Autumn fashion in a complex, connected everyday moment. A reference-guided fashion subject is portrayed as a generated adult woman working on a wind-loosened stage backdrop at a small rooftop theatre rehearsal. Her visible face and hair cues follow the supplied image: a softly tapering face, rounded dark eyes, small straight nose, full lips, short black bob around the jaw and a fine wispy forehead fringe. Her concentrated downward attention and quietly parted lips keep everyday attraction a subtle part of an absorbed practical moment. She is wearing autumn layers: an open cropped cocoa-and-charcoal flecked tweed jacket over a short wine-red buttoned cardigan and cream rib-knit roll-neck, a knee-length checked wool skirt with deep box pleats, and dark chocolate knee boots. The cardigan's buttoned lower edge meets the skirt waistband, between the jacket's higher open fronts. Cream knit appears above the outer collars and beyond both sleeve cuffs. The cardigan hem and the top of the checked pleats remain in the clear central interval between the jacket fronts. On the working tweed sleeve, the garment's fabric texture or sheen is distinguishable in the raised flecked surface. Its folds originate at a seam joint or pulling contact, at the visible stitched line crossing her bent right elbow. Their fold direction agrees with the body's action or pose as short compression ridges open from that stitched bend along the reaching sleeve. The folds preserve the garment silhouette and closure, keeping the same intact sleeve cuff and continuous open jacket fronts. Both booted feet rest on the dry wooden deck with a stable stagger and soft knees. Her torso stays balanced over the feet. Turn her upper body slightly toward the camera and rotate the working elbow outward enough to show its stitched seam while keeping the right forearm aimed toward the waist-high brass ring fixed to the rail on her right. The woman draws the canvas corner through the brass ring while her left hand holds the folded edge. Her right thumb and fingers grip the emerging doubled cloth several centimetres beyond the ring; her left hand grips the incoming folded strip a few centimetres before its rim. The two cuffs, wrists and hands are separately traceable. Between the hands, the folded strip visibly crosses the open center of the ring, with a short incoming segment and an emerging segment separated by the metal rim. The canvas corner is continuous with the blue-painted backdrop and emerges beneath the circular brass ring as a folded hanging tail. The upper painted cloth still bows while its lower held corner gathers, leaving the next knot unfinished. Use a front three-quarter environmental full-length view at waist height that reveals the open center of the ring, the working elbow seam, the cardigan-skirt junction, face and both boots in one vertical 4:5 frame. Keep the hands separated from the ring rim and from the waist landmark in projection. Rehearsal chairs and a chalk stage mark remain behind the working subject. Cool afternoon skylight with a small warm doorway lamp edge describes natural skin and distinct fabric surfaces, with the person and contact plane crisp against a softly receding parapet.

definitions.principle: These creative definitions guide agent-owned choices within requester meaning, not clinical classifications. Zero/off disables added treatment, never removes explicitly requested content or artistic judgment. Expression levels describe prominence in the whole image; creativity levels describe interpretive freedom. Neither measures exposure percentages, detail quotas, quality scores, or native image-model parameters. Intensity and expression are separate choices; higher intensity does not prescribe a garment, material or expression category. Creativity leaves style, extra props and surreal treatment open to the request and artistic judgment. Emphasis directs only active sensual and fetish axes without changing their intensities. Popular permits familiar appeal without requiring trend search; overt is an available expression, not the mandatory meaning of level three. Choose a coherent expression suited to this particular scene. Sensual and fetish may share the same expressive choice.

authorial_core.baseline_prompt_en: Autumn fashion in a complex, connected everyday moment. A reference-guided fashion subject is portrayed as a generated adult woman working on a wind-loosened stage backdrop at a small rooftop theatre rehearsal. Her visible face and hair cues follow the supplied image: a softly tapering face, rounded dark eyes, small straight nose, full lips, short black bob around the jaw and a fine wispy forehead fringe. Her concentrated downward attention and quietly parted lips keep everyday attraction a subtle part of an absorbed practical moment. She is wearing autumn layers: an open cropped cocoa-and-charcoal flecked tweed jacket over a short wine-red buttoned cardigan and cream rib-knit roll-neck, a knee-length checked wool skirt with deep box pleats, and dark chocolate knee boots. The cardigan's buttoned lower edge meets the skirt waistband, between the jacket's higher open fronts. Cream knit appears above the outer collars and beyond both sleeve cuffs. The cardigan hem and the top of the checked pleats remain in the clear central interval between the jacket fronts. On the working tweed sleeve, the garment's fabric texture or sheen is distinguishable in the raised flecked surface. Its folds originate at a seam joint or pulling contact, at the visible stitched line crossing her bent right elbow. Their fold direction agrees with the body's action or pose as short compression ridges open from that stitched bend along the reaching sleeve. The folds preserve the garment silhouette and closure, keeping the same intact sleeve cuff and continuous open jacket fronts. Both booted feet rest on the dry wooden deck with a stable stagger and soft knees. Her torso stays balanced over the feet. Turn her upper body slightly toward the camera and rotate the working elbow outward enough to show its stitched seam while keeping the right forearm aimed toward the waist-high brass ring fixed to the rail on her right. The woman draws the canvas corner through the brass ring while her left hand holds the folded edge. Her right thumb and fingers grip the emerging doubled cloth several centimetres beyond the ring; her left hand grips the incoming folded strip a few centimetres before its rim. The two cuffs, wrists and hands are separately traceable. Between the hands, the folded strip visibly crosses the open center of the ring, with a short incoming segment and an emerging segment separated by the metal rim. The canvas corner is continuous with the blue-painted backdrop and emerges beneath the circular brass ring as a folded hanging tail. The upper painted cloth still bows while its lower held corner gathers, leaving the next knot unfinished. Use a front three-quarter environmental full-length view at waist height that reveals the open center of the ring, the working elbow seam, the cardigan-skirt junction, face and both boots in one vertical 4:5 frame. Keep the hands separated from the ring rim and from the waist landmark in projection. Rehearsal chairs and a chalk stage mark remain behind the working subject. Cool afternoon skylight with a small warm doorway lamp edge describes natural skin and distinct fabric surfaces, with the person and contact plane crisp against a softly receding parapet.
